body:
Good catch, @o-alexandre-felipe :+1: Thx for reporting!

Indeed, according to https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/31198#issuecomment-505941484, we need to update the dependency in [aio/tools/examples/shared/package.json][1]. Would you be interested in making this change and submitting a pull request?

[1]: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/c6b29f4c6d23b1510db3434cb030203d5bdea119/aio/tools/examples/shared/package.json#L35
Ok @sparshag21, I wish you a good contribution :)-
@sparshag21, if you're still planning on doing this, will you tag me?

Reading the issue description again, I now realize there are two issues discussed here:

1. An outdated version of `angular-in-memory-web-api` in the examples' `package.json`.
2. The `@angular/elements` dependency missing from the `elements' example's `package.json`.

The first issue has already been fixed (see https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/393398e6f#diff-835d685609901b14699e46f15601e9f0).

For the second, we need to introduce a new `elements` example type and specify that the `elements` example is of that type. We actually had such a type in the past, but it was removed in 661a57d9e. So, we basically need to re-introduce it.

It is likely not a good first contribution candidate, but if anyone wants to take a stub at it, we basically need similar changes to 1c533c913 (the commit that introduced it originally), except that instead of a custom `aio/tools/examples/boilerplate/element/tsconfig.json` we now need a custom `aio/tools/examples/boilerplate/element/package.json` (which lists `@angular/elements` as a dependency). This would be very similar to the `package.json` for [`service-worker` example type][1] (except that we would have `@angular/elements` instead of `@angular/service-worker`).

[1]: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/c88305d2e/aio/tools/examples/shared/boilerplate/service-worker/package.json

Can I take a stab at the `@angular/elements` dependency fix. The explanation given by @gkalpak  of what needs to be done seems clear and I would love to do this as my first open source contribution, as well as for Hacktoberfest 😄

Sure, go for it, @yallen011. (fyi @kapunahelewong (who's currently assigned) to avoid duplication of work)
@yallen011, feel free to ping @kapunahelewong or me if you have questions/run into difficulties.
